items.title: Fahmi: New legislation to replace UUCA will exclude provisions affecting student freedom
items.summary: KUALA LUMPUR, Aug 19 — The new legislation that will replace the Universities and University Colleges Act (UUCA) 1971 will not restrict the freedom of students or undergraduates. Government spokesman Datuk Seri Fahmi Fadzil assured that the new legislative Bill will instead focus on the administration and management aspects of universities as well as university colleges. He said Prime Minister Datuk Seri Anwar Ibrahim had told the Cabinet that matters involving students and undergraduates will be excluded following the government’s intention to abolish UUCA 1971 as announced last weekend.

items.title: Finance Ministry witness says PMO involved in Jana Wibawa procurement process, but no order to select KCJ Engineering
items.summary: Today, Zamzuri referred to Muhyiddin’s November 13, 2020 letter to the finance minister, which contained a list of 54 proposed companies for 54 proposed Jana Wibawa projects, including KCJ Engineering Sdn Bhd. At that time, Zamzuri was secretary of the Finance Ministry’s government procurement division. Based on this list, Zamzuri agreed that the PMO was involved before the process to evaluate contractors for three of the Jana Wibawa projects, which were eventually awarded to KCJ Engineering Sdn Bhd, Nepturis Sdn Bhd and Sutracom Sdn Bhd.

items.title: PM has no power to direct project awards, High Court told
items.summary: Deputy public prosecutor Datuk Wan Shaharuddin Wan Ladin asked Zamzuri whether the Prime Minister's Office (PMO) was involved in the procurement and assessment process for KCJ Engineering Sdn Bhd. Zamzuri agreed that KCJ Engineering had initially failed the preliminary assessment by the Jana Wibawa Contractor Evaluation Committee. Zamzuri: Yes.

items.title: DAP's equal allocations call not discussed at Cabinet meeting - Fahmi
items.summary: PUTRAJAYA: DAP's call for equal constituency development allocations for all members of parliament was not discussed at today's Cabinet meeting, government spokesman Datuk Seri Fahmi Fadzil said. The communications minister said Prime Minister Datuk Seri Anwar Ibrahim was aware of the matter adding that it may be discussed by the Cabinet at a later date. Gobind also urged the government to enact a legislation to institutionalise equal allocations and remove political discretion from the distribution of constituency development funds.

items.title: Police probe whether stress played role in Hulu Selangor teacher’s death
items.summary: SHAH ALAM, Aug 19 — Police are continuing investigations into the death of a female teacher who was found unconscious at a school in Hulu Selangor late last month. Selangor Police chief Datuk Shazeli Kahar said investigators were examining various factors, including whether stress played a role, in the case which has so far been classified as a sudden death report (SDR). Separately, Shazeli said police were investigating allegations that a workshop in Kampung Bukit Kapar, Klang, which had been linked to foreign nationals suspected of dismantling and selling vehicle parts, was set on fire to destroy evidence.

items.title: Motorcycle noise complaint sparks fight, 3 injured in Penampang
items.summary: PENAMPANG: A complaint about a motorcycle's loud engine noise escalated into a fight that left three men injured at Kampung Muhibbah, Petagas, here last night. Penampang district police chief Superintendent Sammy Newton said police received information about a fight involving a group of people who were gathered and playing carrom outside a house. He said initial investigations found that the 37-year-old suspect had ridden through the area on a motorcycle, producing a loud engine noise.

items.title: Anwar hails Bukit Mertajam Hospital's global green recognition
items.summary: GEORGE TOWN: Prime Minister Datuk Seri Anwar Ibrahim has congratulated Bukit Mertajam Hospital on its global recognition as a Green Hospital. The hospital is the only one in Malaysia to be listed among the world's top 250 hospitals for sustainability initiatives. Bukit Mertajam Hospital has been recognised among the world's top 250 greenest hospitals in Newsweek and Statista's World's Greenest Hospitals 2026 ranking, making it the only Malaysian hospital to receive this international recognition for climate action and environmental sustainability.

items.title: FB, TikTok account for 92pct of scam content flagged for removal
items.summary: PUTRAJAYA: Some 127,568 scam-related online content items have been flagged for removal as of today, with Facebook and TikTok accounting for 53 per cent and 39 per cent respectively. Government spokesman Datuk Seri Fahmi Fadzil said the content included false claims, such as unannounced additional Sumbangan Asas Rahmah (Sara) payments purportedly from the Finance Ministry. He said the figure represented 27 per cent of the total requests for content removal.

items.title: Solarvest Q1 earnings up 19.8pct on stronger revenue, associate contributions
items.summary: KUALA LUMPUR: Solarvest Holdings Bhd's net profit rose 19.8 per cent to RM19.02 million in the first quarter ended June 30, 2026, from RM15.87 million a year earlier, driven by higher revenue and increased contributions from associates and joint ventures. Revenue grew 13.2 per cent to RM155.93 million from RM137.74 million, mainly supported by utility-scale projects, including multiple Large Scale Solar 5 (LSS5) developments and ongoing works under the Corporate Green Power Programme. As at end-June, Malaysia had reached nearly 33 per cent installed RE capacity, reflecting continued progress in clean energy infrastructure and the country's energy transition.

items.title: Immigration lorry crash: Two drivers remanded for probe
items.summary: KUALA LUMPUR: Police have remanded two drivers involved in a fatal collision involving an Immigration Department lorry that killed a father and his two daughters along Jalan Sultan Ismail early today. Kuala Lumpur Traffic Enforcement and Investigation Department chief Assistant Commissioner Mohd Zamzuri Mohd Isa said the drivers of the Proton Saga and the lorry were remanded for a day to facilitate investigations. "We have remanded the driver of the Proton Saga and the driver of the lorry for a day," he said when contacted.

items.title: Miros: Road safety not just public safety issue, but economic priority
items.summary: KUALA LUMPUR: Reducing road fatalities is not merely a public safety agenda but a strategic investment to safeguard national productivity and economic growth, says the Malaysian Institute of Road Safety Research (Miros). In a statement, Miros clarified that the estimated RM30 billion in socioeconomic losses from road crashes last year was calculated using the Value of Statistical Life (VOSL) methodology, based on fatality and serious injury data recorded by the police. "The findings underscore that efforts to reduce road crashes are not merely a road safety agenda, but a strategic investment to safeguard productivity, public wellbeing and the country's economic growth," it said.

items.title: Only 352 Malaysians have applied for 3D jobs so far on MyFutureJobs portal
items.summary: PUTRAJAYA: Despite thousands of positions offered in the 'dirty, dangerous and difficult' (3D) jobs sector, only 352 applications have come from Malaysians so far on the MyFutureJobs website. Human Resources Minister Datuk Seri R. Ramanan said that while priority for the jobs is given to Malaysians, the numbers showed a gap between available jobs and the take-up rate by Malaysians. "When the jobs are offered on MyFutureJobs, and no Malaysians come forward to take them, only then would we open them up to foreign workers, refugees or others," he said.

items.title: Sandakan declares fire disaster after 28 homes destroyed on Pulau Nunuyan Laut
items.summary: SANDAKAN, Aug 19 — The Sandakan District Disaster Management Committee (JPBD) today declared a fire disaster in the district following a blaze that destroyed 28 houses at Pulau Nunuyan Laut early this morning. Sandakan JPBD chairman Datuk Walter Kenson said the declaration was made at 9am based on reports and information received from agencies on the ground. In a statement here today, he said a temporary relief centre (PPS) was opened at Masjid Al Fattah, Kampung Nunuyan Laut, at 10am following the declaration.

items.title: Selangor govt refers religious school sexual assault case to police
items.summary: State Islamic Affairs executive councillor Dr Mohammad Fahmi Ngah said the state government viewed the matter seriously and expressed regret over the incident. Fahmi said he was confident the Selangor Islamic Religious Department (JAIS) would take appropriate action under existing laws, including reviewing the school's registration if necessary. He said JAIS had taken measures to prevent misconduct involving teachers and students, teachers among themselves, and students.

items.title: Ramkarpal urges Sanusi to respect Federal Court ruling on Kedah gambling ban
items.summary: GEORGE TOWN: DAP lawmaker Ramkarpal Singh has urged Kedah Menteri Besar Datuk Seri Muhammad Sanusi Md Nor to respect the Federal Court ruling on the state's gambling premises ban. The Bukit Gelugor member of parliament's call came after Sanusi said the state government respected the Federal Court's decision to dismiss Kedah's application for leave to appeal against a ruling declaring its ban on gambling premises unlawful. Ramkarpal, who is also DAP National Legal Bureau chairman, said Sanusi should focus on more effective enforcement measures to address Muslims participating in gambling activities.

items.title: Thai worker charged with sexually assaulting teenage cousin
items.summary: He was accused of committing a similar offence against the victim at the same location and time on June 1 under the second charge. Deputy Public Prosecutor Syazalia Che Suhaimin prosecuted, while the accused was unrepresented. The accused was denied bail.

items.title: Haze eases for now, but could return within days, says MetMalaysia
items.summary: PUTRAJAYA, Aug 19 — Humid weather over the past few days has helped ease haze in the Klang Valley and Sarawak, but conditions could deteriorate again in the near future. Malaysian Meteorological Department (MetMalaysia) director-general Mohd Hisham Mohd Anip said hot and dry conditions were expected to return within days, with the country still in the Southwest Monsoon season until the end of September. During the Southwest Monsoon, lower humidity contributes to reduced rainfall and more days without rain, Mohd Hisham said.

items.title: Police probe Shah Alam school bullying, 17-year-old suspect out on bail
items.summary: SHAH ALAM: Police have opened an investigation into a bullying incident involving a 15-year-old student at a secondary school here, with the 17-year-old suspect released on bail after being remanded. Selangor police chief Datuk Shazeli Kahar said the case was being investigated under Sections 506 and 323 of the Penal Code for criminal intimidation and voluntarily causing hurt. The victim's mother, Nurhaswaty Zamani, 43, said her son, Adryz Adrian, suffered head and ear injuries following the alleged incident.

items.title: Cabinet did not discuss Anwar's Taiwan remarks, says Fahmi
items.summary: PUTRAJAYA: The cabinet did not discuss Prime Minister Datuk Seri Anwar Ibrahim's remarks on Taiwan, which drew a strong rebuke from Taipei, says government spokesman Datuk Seri Fahmi Fadzil. Fahmi was asked about a statement issued by Taiwan's Foreign Ministry yesterday criticising Anwar's remarks during a recent interview with Al Jazeera. In the interview, Anwar expressed support for the One China policy and said historical factors should be considered when examining Taiwan's relationship with China.

items.title: [UPDATED] Cabinet approves National Border Plan for immediate action
items.summary: PUTRAJAYA: The cabinet has approved the Comprehensive National Border Plan for immediate implementation, says government spokesman Datuk Seri Fahmi Fadzil. The Communications Minister said the plan was presented by the Home Ministry and Transport Ministry at today's cabinet meeting. "There are several matters that were presented by both the Home Ministry and Transport Ministry.

items.title: Fire disaster declared in Sandakan after 28 houses destroyed
items.summary: SANDAKAN: The Sandakan District Disaster Management Committee today declared a fire disaster in the district after a blaze destroyed 28 houses at Pulau Nunuyan Laut early this morning. Its chairman Datuk Walter Kenson said the declaration was made at 9am based on reports and information received from agencies on the ground. In a statement, he said a temporary relief centre (PPS) was opened at Masjid Al Fattah, Kampung Nunuyan Laut, at 10am following the declaration.

items.title: Govt urged to clarify legal status of liquid nicotine after appeal withdrawal
items.summary: KUALA LUMPUR: The government must clarify the legal status of liquid and gel nicotine used in vape products following its withdrawal of an appeal against a High Court ruling that invalidated the exemption of nicotine from the poisons list. Malaysian Council for Tobacco Control (MCTC) secretary-general Muhammad Sha'ani Abdullah said the government should also clarify the relationship between the Poisons Act and the Control of Smoking Products for Public Health Act 2024 (Act 852) to avoid conflict in the legal framework governing nicotine and vaping. "The government must review the compatibility of Act 852 with the Poisons Act, including all subsidiary regulations relating to vaping.

items.title: Khaled: Regional uncertainty, emerging threats underpin higher defence spending
items.summary: KUALA LUMPUR: Malaysia's push for higher defence spending is driven not only by regional security developments but also by emerging threats including cyberattacks, electromagnetic threats and mass misinformation. Defence Minister Datuk Seri Mohamed Khaled Nordin said these evolving challenges required Malaysia to enhance its defence assets and capabilities. Khaled was speaking following Prime Minister Datuk Seri Anwar Ibrahim's call for higher defence spending and stronger defence capabilities in Sabah, amid concerns over US military expansion in the Philippines.

items.title: [UPDATED] Cabinet orders study on proposed hybrid GST-SST system
items.summary: PUTRAJAYA: The cabinet has directed the Finance Ministry to conduct a comprehensive study into a proposed hybrid Goods and Services Tax (GST)-Sales and Services Tax (SST) system. Government spokesman Datuk Seri Fahmi Fadzil said Finance Minister II Datuk Seri Amir Hamzah Azizan had been given time to prepare a report before bringing the matter back to the cabinet for further discussion. Anwar said, however, that the existing SST framework remained the basis of the country's tax system and that he did not support a broad-based tax that would burden those who currently did not pay tax.

items.title: [UPDATED] Anwar orders review of TalentCorp's handling of doctors' return applications
items.summary: PUTRAJAYA: Prime Minister Datuk Seri Anwar Ibrahim has instructed the Human Resources Ministry to review TalentCorp's handling of applications, including those from doctors seeking to return to Malaysia to serve. Communications Minister Datuk Seri Fahmi Fadzil said Anwar had directed the ministry to report to the cabinet on applications received, processing times, approvals and rejections. He said the review followed several matters raised with Anwar by the Malaysian Medical Council (MMC).

items.title: ‘No need to escalate’: Selangor police urge public against gathering at court over Rocky case
items.summary: SHAH ALAM, Aug 19 — Selangor police chief Datuk Shazeli Kahar today reportedly urged the public not to hold a gathering when a man linked to the death of a dog named Rocky appears in court tomorrow, saying the legal process is already under way. According to The Star , Shazeli said police had completed their investigation, identified those responsible and received instructions for charges to be brought. He reportedly said members of the public who wished to witness the proceedings could attend as the court’s public gallery would be open.

items.title: Rocky's death: Public advised against holding rallies, demonstrations ahead of charges tomorrow
items.summary: SHAH ALAM: Selangor police chief Datuk Shazeli Kahar today advised the public against holding rallies or demonstrations over the death of a dog during an enforcement operation in Port Klang last month. He said police had completed their investigation and identified those responsible, with charges expected to be brought at the Klang magistrate's court tomorrow. Shazeli said the charges followed instructions from the deputy public prosecutor's office after the investigation was completed.

items.title: Malaysia must strengthen maritime logistics as Asean trade surges
items.summary: KUALA LUMPUR: Malaysia needs to address gaps across its maritime logistics and supply chain ecosystem to ensure its ports are able to handle rising cargo volumes driven by trade shift to the Asean region, said industry experts. MTT Shipping and Logistics Bhd managing director and co-founder Ooi Lean Hin said Asean has emerged as one of the biggest beneficiaries of the trade shift, driven by supply chain realignments as China diversifies its market away from the West. MORE TO COME © New Straits Times Press (M) Bhd

items.title: New law to replace Auku will exclude student matters, says Fahmi
items.summary: PUTRAJAYA: Any legislation replacing the Universities and University Colleges Act 1971 (Auku) will focus on university administration and management, while matters involving students and undergraduates will be excluded. Government spokesman Datuk Seri Fahmi Fadzil said Prime Minister Datuk Seri Anwar Ibrahim had informed the Cabinet today of the government's intention to abolish Auku. He said he opposed special laws specifically designed to restrict university students.

items.title: Xavier Jayakumar corruption probe closed in 2024 due to insufficient evidence, says MACC
items.summary: PUTRAJAYA, Aug 19 — A corruption investigation involving former minister Datuk Dr Xavier Jayakumar reportedly was closed in 2024 after prosecutors found insufficient evidence to charge him, the Malaysian Anti-Corruption Commission (MACC) said today. Utusan Malaysia reported that MACC said two investigation papers had been opened in 2021 under Section 16(a)(A) of the MACC Act 2009, with the relevant facts, documents and evidence subsequently examined. “The deputy public prosecutor decided to classify the case as ‘closed and filed’ in 2024 because there was insufficient evidence to charge Datuk Dr Xavier,” the commission was quoted as saying.

items.title: Kampar father, 2 daughters killed in Jalan Sultan Ismail crash identified
items.summary: KUALA LUMPUR: The three family members killed in a crash involving an Immigration Department lorry along Jalan Sultan Ismail early today have been identified. Kuala Lumpur Traffic Enforcement and Investigation Department chief Assistant Commissioner Mohd Zamzuri Mohd Isa said the family was from Kampar, Perak. The victims were identified as Shaik Mohd Firdaus Shaikh Yahya, 53, and his daughters, Siti Nor Sazlin, 25, and Siti Darwisyah Auni, 12.

items.title: KL police identify father and two daughters killed in Maju Junction crash; nephew says family was visiting relatives
items.summary: KUALA LUMPUR, Aug 19 — Police have identified the three family members killed in the early morning crash involving a Malaysian Immigration Department lorry on Jalan Sultan Ismail. Kuala Lumpur Traffic Investigation and Enforcement Department chief ACP Mohd Zamzuri Mohd Isa said they were Shaik Mohd Firdaus Shaikh Yahya, 53, and his two daughters, Siti Nor Sazlin, 25, and Siti Darwisyah Auni, 12. Also present was Kuala Lumpur Immigration director Hamsha Injau.

items.title: Two UNHCR card holders charged over house break-ins
items.summary: MUAR: Two Rohingya men linked to a string of house break-ins in the district were charged at the Magistrate's Court today. Jamal faced three charges while Ramzan faced one. Ramzan was granted RM4,000 bail with two sureties.

items.title: Lotte Chemical Titan neither confirms nor denies parent's potential stake sale
items.summary: KUALA LUMPUR: Lotte Chemical Titan Holding Bhd has neither confirmed nor denied reports that its South Korean parent is looking to sell its stake in the company, after news of the potential sale sent its shares up more than 30 per cent. In a clarification filed with Bursa Malaysia, the company said Lotte Chemical Corp (LCC), which owns 75 per cent of Lotte Chemical Titan, is considering various strategic measures concerning the company, but has made no decision thus far. The Korea Economic Daily report said Lotte Chemical Titan was the primary target for disposal, with LCC reviewing market conditions and potential buyers.

items.title: Malaysian passport ranked fourth strongest globally
items.summary: KUALA LUMPUR: The Malaysian passport has been ranked the fourth strongest in the world, with holders granted visa-free, visa-on-arrival or electronic travel authorisation access to 174 destinations. "Of these, 121 destinations, or 61.1 per cent, offer Malaysians visa-free entry. The report said Malaysian passport holders have access to eight destinations via electronic travel authorisation or equivalent digital systems, including the United Kingdom, Australia, South Korea, New Zealand and Seychelles.

items.title: Cigarettes hidden in coconut husks: Kelantan Customs foils RM1.37mil smuggling attempt
items.summary: RANTAU PANJANG: The Kelantan Customs Department has foiled an attempt to smuggle 1.96 million sticks of cigarettes believed to have been brought in from China, with the total value of the seizure, including duties and taxes, estimated at RM1.37 million. Kelantan Customs director Mohd Hisham Mohd Nor said the seizure was made by the Rantau Panjang Enforcement Branch Operations Team in Bachok on July 17 under Ops Asap Cino. Hisham said the team also detected a Toyota Unser at the same location carrying 253,600 sticks of white cigarettes, estimated to be worth RM178,027.20, including duties and taxes.

items.title: Ahead of Budget 2027, higher education students call for expanded assistance to manage rising living expenses
items.summary: KUALA LUMPUR, Aug 19 — Ahead of the tabling of Budget 2027, higher education students are hoping the government will expand financial assistance to help them cope with rising costs of living. Besides increases to existing aid such as Sumbangan Tunai Rahmah (STR) and Sumbangan Asas Rahmah (SARA), students are calling for new measures to ease their daily expenses. Increasing National Higher Education Fund Corporation (PTPTN) loans was not a complete solution, he said, calling on the government to provide targeted assistance or subsidies to help cover education and living costs without adding to students’ financial burden after graduation.

items.title: Defending our sovereignty beyond the battlefield
items.summary: But sovereignty was never a one-time achievement. A purely territorial idea of sovereignty is no longer enough. A civil servant who resists corruption defends sovereignty.

items.title: Govt withdraws nicotine appeal, cites existing vape regulations
items.summary: He said this was among the main reasons for the government's decision to discontinue its appeal against a High Court ruling regarding the removal of nicotine from the poisons list. Dusuki said the decision was made after Health Minister Datuk Seri Dr Dzulkefly Ahmad studied the High Court's grounds of judgment. On May 15, High Court judge Datuk Aliza Sulaiman ruled that exempting nicotine from the poisons list under the Poisons (Amendment of Poisons List) Order 2023 was irrational and ultra vires Section 6 of the Poisons Act 1952.

items.title: Shah Alam police receive report on Form Three student at risk of hearing loss after alleged bullying
items.summary: SHAH ALAM, Aug 19 — Police have confirmed receiving a report regarding an incident involving a Form Three student who claimed to have been bullied to the extent of being at risk of hearing loss at a secondary school here last week. Selangor police chief Datuk Shazeli Kahar said the 17-year-old suspect had been detained and released on police bail pending completion of investigations. Yesterday, the media reported that a Form Three male student had suffered injuries to his neck and nape and was at risk of hearing loss after allegedly being bullied and assaulted at a secondary school here last week.

items.title: Quizzed on China-Taiwan relations, Anwar says he would use force if needed to prevent Malaysia from breaking up (VIDEO)
items.summary: KUCHING, Aug 19 — Prime Minister Datuk Seri Anwar Ibrahim believes he would use force to prevent any province from breaking away from the Federation of Malaysia. Sreenivasan: So, you would use force? Anwar: Yes.

items.title: Melaka Sentral refutes claim terminal has been without air‑conditioning for months
items.summary: Its general manager Zulhafni Md Rahis said records and monitoring showed that the temperature inside the terminal remained under control. He said MSSB regularly monitors and maintains the air-conditioning system to ensure the comfort of visitors and smooth terminal operations. “We are always open to complaints and feedback from traders and visitors regarding comfort and facilities at the terminal.

items.title: KL police say personal grudge behind petrol attack on woman at Kepong lottery outlet
items.summary: Kuala Lumpur police chief Comm Datuk Fadil Marsus said this when confirming details of the case, according to a report by The Star. He said officers arrested a 59-year-old local man in Kepong yesterday to assist investigations. He said the case remains under investigation.

items.title: Works Ministry seeks bigger 2027 development budget to bolster infrastructure plans, says Ahmad Maslan
items.summary: KUALA LUMPUR, Aug 19 — The Ministry of Works (KKR) is seeking a higher allocation in the 2027 Budget compared with the previous year to ensure the nation’s infrastructure development agenda continues to be strengthened. Deputy Works Minister Datuk Seri Ahmad Maslan said the ministry hoped to remain one of the main recipients of Development Expenditure (DE) allocations in the government’s annual budget. “Year after year, out of the 28 ministries, KKR receives the largest development allocation.

items.title: Consular assistance to Malaysians detained abroad does not grant immunity, says legal expert
items.summary: KUALA LUMPUR, Aug 19 — Malaysians are reminded that consular assistance provided by Malaysian embassies or High Commissions to citizens detained abroad does not grant them immunity from the laws of the host country. Instead, the consular role is to ensure that the detainees’ welfare and rights are protected, said Universiti Teknologi MARA (UiTM) Shah Alam, Faculty of Law, Advocacy and Dispute Resolution Centre head Mimi Sintia Mohd Bajury. “Consular officials also monitor court proceedings to uphold the accused’s right to a fair trial, in accordance with the host country’s laws.

items.title: KL police dispose of RM15m in seized drugs to ensure integrity of case exhibits
items.summary: KUALA LUMPUR, Aug 19 — The Kuala Lumpur police today disposed of various types of drugs worth over RM15 million seized during operations across the capital, as part of efforts to ensure the integrity and proper management of case exhibits. Kuala Lumpur police chief Datuk Fadil Marsus said the disposal involved 5,022 case exhibits from 4,884 investigation papers for which court proceedings had concluded between 2007 and 2025. Fadil said the solid drugs disposed of totalled 544 kilogrammes, comprising methamphetamine, ketamine, heroin, cocaine and cannabis, while liquid drugs exceeded 900 litres, including ketum liquid.

items.title: Firefighters save 162 homes after blaze destroys 28 stilt houses at Pulau Nunuyan Laut in Sandakan
items.summary: SANDAKAN, Aug 19 — A total of 28 non-permanent stilt houses were destroyed in a fire at Kampung Nunuyan Laut, Nunuyan Laut Island, here early today. The Sabah Fire and Rescue Department (JBPM) Operations Centre, in a statement, said no injuries or fatalities were reported in the incident. “The Fire and Rescue Department received an emergency call at 3.50am and subsequently deployed the Sandakan Fire and Rescue Station team, assisted by a Malaysian Maritime Enforcement Agency (MMEA) boat, to the scene, located 18 kilometres away.

items.title: Police receive 375 tactical e‑bikes worth RM8m for faster, quieter border patrols
items.summary: KUALA LUMPUR, Aug 19 — The Royal Malaysia Police (PDRM) has received 375 All Terrain Tactical Assault E-Bikes (ATEBs) worth more than RM8 million to strengthen security along the country’s borders. Inspector-General of Police Tan Sri Mohd Khalid Ismail said the electric tactical bikes would be deployed to states bordering Thailand, including Perlis, Kedah, Kelantan and Perak, as well as Sabah and Sarawak. He said the ATEBs would enhance the capabilities of police personnel, particularly the General Operations Force (GOF), allowing them to conduct border patrols more quickly, quietly and effectively.

items.title: Malaysians among applicants affected as Australia slows Work and Holiday visa processing
items.summary: KUALA LUMPUR, Aug 19 — Australia has temporarily paused applications from Malaysians seeking their first Work and Holiday visa under subclass 462. Australia’s ABC News reported yesterday that Malaysia is among 24 countries — almost all under visa stream — whose applications have been paused. The cap reportedly applies only to first subclass 462 visas, while second and third Work and Holiday visas are not subject to country quotas.

items.title: Kelantan police vow firm action against ‘tonto’ used to block enforcement in human‑smuggling cases
items.summary: KOTA BHARU, Aug 19 — Police will take firm action against human-smuggling syndicates using ‘tonto’ to obstruct enforcement vehicles, following a recent incident in which two General Operations Force (GOF) personnel were hit while carrying out their duties. Kelantan police chief Datuk Mohd Yusoff Mamat said the incident showed that the syndicates were becoming increasingly bold, stressing that such actions would not be tolerated. Mohd Yusoff said police had also detected human-smuggling activities using sea routes and rivers along the Kelantan coast, adding that enforcement agencies would remain vigilant against such operations.

items.title: MB: Pahang reports end of recorded hardcore poverty, with 2,913 households lifted and overall poverty down 30pc
items.summary: KUANTAN, Aug 19 — Pahang’s hardcore poverty was brought to an end on Feb 19, with all 2,913 heads of household recorded in the Jan 15, 2026 figure removed from the status, said Pahang Menteri Besar Datuk Seri Wan Rosdy Wan Ismail. He said the state had also recorded a 30 per cent reduction in poverty, with 4,263 of the 14,210 heads of household classified as poor on June 5 subsequently removed from the category. Wan Rosdy said key factors behind the achievement included targeted assistance, initiatives and interventions provided by the state and federal governments and relevant agencies, as well as changes in household income and household size.

items.title: Immigration Dept opens internal probe after fatal KL crash that killed three
items.summary: In a statement posted on Facebook, Immigration director-general Datuk Zakaria Shaaban said the department would give its full cooperation to the police in determining the cause of the accident. Zakaria said the department would also conduct an internal investigation into compliance with standard operating procedures and safety aspects involving the operation of department vehicles to ensure the matter was thoroughly examined. Zakaria said the department viewed the incident seriously and would take appropriate action based on the findings of the police investigation and its internal probe.

items.title: More workplace subsidies, tax incentives needed to support breastfeeding mothers, says Yeo Bee Yin
items.summary: PETALING JAYA, Aug 19 — The government should provide more subsidies and tax incentives to companies to set up breastfeeding rooms and childcare facilities in the workplace. “This includes breastfeeding rooms or multipurpose rooms where mothers can pump their milk, as well as childcare facilities in the workplace,” she said during a panel discussion titled ‘Realities of Breastfeeding’, held in conjunction with Toshiba Lifestyle Malaysia’s ‘World Breastfeeding Month 2026: Empowering Every Mother’s Journey’ event here yesterday. “Every child is different.

items.title: Investment firm director previously charged with CBT now faces RM13.4m money‑laundering counts
items.summary: KUALA LUMPUR, Aug 19 — An investment company director, previously charged with criminal breach of trust, was brought before the Sessions Court here again today to face 10 charges of receiving RM13.4 million in proceeds from unlawful activities. Datuk Norliza Tajudin, 54, pleaded not guilty after all the charges were read out individually before Judge Suzana Hussin. “The prosecution also applies for this case to be tried jointly with the previous case (criminal breach of trust) in this court,” she said.

items.title: Nilai private university CFO accused of RM6.56m CBT linked to IRB duty payments
items.summary: SEREMBAN, Aug 19 — A chief financial officer (CFO) of a private university in Nilai pleaded not guilty in the Sessions Court here today to allegedly committing criminal breach of trust involving RM6.56 million in company funds between September 2025 and April this year. Noraini Aripin, 55, entered the plea after the charge was read out to her before Judge Datin M. Kunasundary Marimuthu. Deputy Public Prosecutor Syairah Aqilah Khalil sought bail of RM100,000 with two sureties, with the accused also required to surrender her passport to the court and report to the Negeri Sembilan Malaysian Anti-Corruption Commission (MACC) office each month.

items.title: Former UBB Investment Bank CEO pleads not guilty to RM139.8m cheating charge
items.summary: Razlan Raghazli, 43, the former CEO of UBB Investment Bank Limited, entered the plea after the charge was read out to him before Judge Azura Alwi. He was charged with cheating the Managing Director and CEO of UBB Amanah Berhad, Aida Aizura Othman, 52, by deceiving her into believing that the payment schedule contained in a UBB Investment Bank Limited letter was in accordance with legal advice. However, the accused allegedly knew that the payment schedule in question actually contradicted the advice provided by the law firm.

items.title: Police: Chinese national detained after allegedly disrupting passengers at KLIA, later admitted to psychiatric ward
items.summary: PETALING JAYA, Aug 19 — A 27-year-old Chinese national who allegedly behaved aggressively towards passengers at Kuala Lumpur International Airport’s Terminal 1 building is believed to be mentally unwell and has been detained for further investigation, police said today. KLIA police chief Assistant Commissioner M Ravi said authorities were alerted to the incident involving the woman at about 1.19pm on August 18, after she allegedly began shouting and disturbing passengers in the terminal's departure hall by running, singing and dancing. "Her partner later told police that she had forgotten to take her prescribed medication," he said.

items.title: Kelana Jaya LRT services back to normal after Putra Heights safety system fault
items.summary: KUALA LUMPUR, Aug 19 — Rapid KL said the Kelana Jaya LRT Line resumed normal operations at 9.19am today after inspection and recovery works at Putra Heights station were completed. The public transport operator said the earlier disruption was caused by a fault involving the station’s safety detection system. Rapid KL said its technical team would continue monitoring the system and train movements to ensure services along the Kelana Jaya Line run smoothly.

items.title: Delays on Kelana Jaya LRT Line after suspected power supply fault
items.summary: KUALA LUMPUR, Aug 19 — Rapid KL said today that services on the Kelana Jaya LRT Line are experiencing delays due to a suspected fault involving a power supply component at Putra Heights station. It said this would also slow train movements at nearby stations and result in longer waiting times for passengers on platforms. Passengers were advised to check Rapid KL’s social media channels or the MyRapid PULSE journey-planning app for the latest updates on Kelana Jaya Line services.

items.title: Saifuddin Nasution hits out at recycled false claims of Home Ministry granting citizenship en masse to foreigners
items.summary: PUTRAJAYA, Aug 19 — Home Minister Datuk Seri Saifuddin Nasution Ismail has denied claims that the Home Ministry (KDN) granted citizenship en masse to foreign nationals and that 1.2 million Chinese nationals had remained in Malaysia. Saifuddin Nasution said the matter had already been explained officially, with the facts documented in earlier statements and media reports. “Use social media responsibly.
